description:
TUTORING CHECKPOINT (one-step Socratic style per .claude/skills/tutor). Goal: teach the author rhoPimpleFoam's pressure-based algorithm from first principles, feeding (a) a new appendix section 'rhoPimpleFoam basic equations' and (b) understanding of op-26w Part 2 (compressibility psi = drho/dp|_h, why frozen isothermal kappa_T ~100x too small in the dome causes the plateau OVERSHOOT).

WHERE WE PAUSED: just wrote the continuous compressible momentum equation d(rho u)/dt + div(rho u u) = -grad(p) + div(mu grad u), labelled 4 terms (time, convection, pressure, viscous). Paused at the anchor question: identify the 3 'transport skeleton' terms (time+convection+viscous -> a_P, a_N, old-time) vs the 1 odd-one-out source (pressure).

NEXT STEPS (in order): (1) discretise momentum term-by-term into a_P u_P = H(u) - grad(p); (2) rearrange -> u_P = HbyA - rAU grad(p), with rAU=1/a_P, HbyA=H(u)/a_P (the code term that confused the author); (3) substitute the face velocity/flux into discrete continuity to BUILD the pressure equation (this closes the 'pressure is the orphan, continuity pins it' thread); (4) return to Part 2: compressibility psi and the plateau overshoot.

ALREADY COVERED & SOLID: Part 1 energy conservation fully derived by author (conservative vs non-conservative ddt differ by h*r; r=discrete continuity residual; rho_cont=rho_old-(dt/V)sum(phi.A) forces r=0). Author also patched the results-section discrete continuity eqn (added V_cell and face area vectors). FV diffusion stencil (rod example, a_P=a_E+a_W, Fick 2nd law) understood.

APPENDIX NOTE: 'rhoPimpleFoam basic equations' is textbook -- cite Jasak thesis, Ferziger & Peric, OpenFOAM programmer's guide; present as re-derived established background, NOT original, to keep novelty claims on the solver fixes.
title: Resume tutoring: rhoPimpleFoam momentum discretisation -> a_P u_P = H - grad(p) -> HbyA -> pressure equation

description:
One of the three HTGR-specific accident sequences, none of which had a bead before 2026-08-11. Source material is already in the archive: kugeler2017vhtr (EUR 28712 EN, open) covers modular-HTR safety and its appendix summarises the key safety experiments.

THE PHYSICS. If the primary boundary fails and air enters a hot graphite core, graphite oxidises: C + O2 -> CO2 and the Boudouard reaction C + CO2 -> 2CO, which is endothermic and becomes significant at high temperature. The consequences that matter are structural degradation of the graphite (it is the core structural material AND the moderator), a chemical heat source, and CO production. Reaction rate is diffusion-limited or chemically-limited depending on temperature, so the regime matters more than the raw Arrhenius constant.

WHY THIS IS TRACTABLE HERE. crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs already carries the reactor and equilibrium machinery this needs, with zero todo!(): gibbs_reactor.rs (multiphase Gibbs energy minimisation), equilibrium_reactor.rs, conversion_reactor.rs, pfr.rs, cstr.rs, plus a full reactions model. Graphite oxidation is a gas-solid equilibrium-plus-kinetics problem of exactly the shape that layer already solves. Reuse it rather than writing fresh chemistry.

Depends on graphite properties (op-jyyp.1) for the solid side and on the bed model for where the heat goes.

Kinetics must come from open published sources with provenance per DATA_POLICY.md. If only a lumped rate is used, say so in the doc comment rather than implying a mechanistic model.
title: HTR-10 accident: air ingress and graphite oxidation

description:
Successor to op-katz. gh:#178 (kept open for this), index gh:#186.

WHERE THE HUNT STANDS. The FHR ring-RPT residual (+4004 pcm) is reproduced on a
MEASURED critical experiment -- ICSBEP LEU-COMP-THERM-008, +2950 +- 61 pcm -- so
it is this code, not the reference deck. Everything else has been excluded by its
own oracle:

  sigma_gamma(E) pointwise         NJOY PENDF, 19 energies        +-0.04 %
  resonance SHAPE                  NJOY PENDF, 6 resonances       0.12 % worst
  infinitely-dilute RI             NJOY PENDF + published         +0.00 %
  SELF-SHIELDED energy treatment   exact slowing-down solution    worst 1.8 sigma
                                   (sigma_b 30-10000 b, I_eff collapsing 11.7x)
  tracking method                  delta vs surface-tracked CSG   18 pcm, and the
                                   two failing systems use one each
  geometry DESCRIPTION             LCT-008 vs the original MCNP   0 mismatches in
                                   deck, pin for pin              11 025 positions
  fast physics / driver            Godiva, Jemima                 +57, +6 pcm
  thermal machinery, homogeneous   HEU-SOL-THERM-009              -18 pcm

WHAT IS LEFT is one thing: what this code does to the flux INSIDE an optically
thick lump. The benchmark pattern says the same -- HEU-SOL-THERM-009 is the one
HOMOGENEOUS thermal case and the one that comes out right; both failing systems
are lumps (1.03 cm UO2 pellets at 176 mfp across at 6.67 eV, and 215 um TRISO
kernels at several mfp).

CANDIDATE MEASUREMENTS, in order of what they would settle:

1. A TWO-REGION oracle. physics::slowing_down gives the exact answer for an
   infinite homogeneous medium. The natural extension is a lump + moderator with
   an exact first-flight escape probability (sphere/cylinder blackness is
   analytic), so the SPATIAL self-shielding can be judged the way the energy part
   just was. Flat-flux collision probability is an approximation, so state the
   accuracy of the reference before leaning on it.
2. The lumping reactivity itself: k_inf of an LCT-008 pin cell, lumped vs
   volume-homogenised with identical inventory. That isolates the spatial term as
   a single number in this code, which can then be compared against equivalence
   theory (Wigner/Carlvik rational approximations, few-percent accurate -- enough
   to detect a gross error, not enough for an 11 % question on its own).
3. Re-read the flight/boundary path for anything that biases the interior flux of
   a highly absorbing region: distance_to_boundary vs collision sampling when
   Sigma_t is ~170 cm-1 (mfp 58 um) against cell dimensions of millimetres to
   centimetres -- i.e. whether any tolerance, nudge or coincidence epsilon in the
   CSG or lattice crossing path is comparable to a mean free path at a resonance
   peak. NUDGE is 1e-9 cm and FP_COINCIDENT similar, both far below 58 um, but
   this is the class of thing left and it has not been looked at with the lump in
   mind.

SIGN AND MAGNITUDE REQUIRED (gh:#182): whatever is proposed must predict LESS
absorption in a lump, i.e. TOO MUCH self-shielding, worth ~11 % of the effective
resonance integral, while leaving a homogeneous medium untouched.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-11 (commit d4b0da78f) SPATIAL HALF MEASURED — also sound. And a boundary
condition that looks exactly like the defect.

LumpCellMc runs a Wigner-Seitz cell through the crate's REAL CSG transport, with
the cell's volume-averaged composition identical to the homogeneous mixture the
deterministic solver answers exactly. Shrink the lump until it is optically
transparent and the cell IS that mixture -- an oracle owing nothing to
equivalence theory or any correlation:

  lump radius / mfp at 6.67 eV    p_esc      vs exact
                        0.103    0.38567     -0.51 %
                        0.343    0.39080     +0.82 %
                        0.856    0.38870     +0.28 %
                        2.569    0.39377     +1.58 %
                        8.564    0.43197    +11.44 %
                       25.693    0.50013    +29.02 %

Textbook. Plus a control: the same walker on a cell whose two regions carry the
HOMOGENISED material, five cell radii 0.03-3 cm (~1 to several hundred reflective
crossings per collision), agrees to <=1.1 % with ZERO lost neutrons.

THE TRAP. The first build used a SPECULARLY reflective sphere and reported +39 %
on a lump 0.034 mfp across, and the same 39-43 % at every size. Specular
reflection off a sphere concentric with the lump CONSERVES b = r sin(theta), so a
neutron with b > R_lump never enters the lump at all. Scale-invariant, and that
flatness is the fingerprint -- self-shielding cannot be flat across two decades
of optical thickness. White closure removes it entirely.

NEW HYPOTHESIS, RIGHT SIGN (this is now the live lead for the pebble):
The FHR pebble is run on a specularly reflective sphere r = 3 cm by BOTH this
crate and its OpenMC reference, fuel zone r < 1.9 cm, so b > 1.9 never reaches
the fuel. Shared, so it cancels in the comparison -- UNLESS the two codes'
specular reflections preserve the invariant to different degrees. Floating-point
drift over hundreds of reflections is enough to randomise it. The code that
preserves it more strongly under-samples its fuel, absorbs less in the U-238
resonances, and reports p and k TOO HIGH. That is this crate (p +8.5 %, k
+4004 pcm).

NEXT MEASUREMENT (cheap): rerun the FHR pebble with a white boundary instead of
the specular sphere and see how far k moves. If it moves thousands of pcm, the
reference case is boundary-dominated and the comparison is fragile; if it barely
moves, the invariant is already being broken in our transport and this lead is
dead.

CAVEAT that keeps this honest: it CANNOT explain LEU-COMP-THERM-008, which is
vacuum-bounded throughout and has no reflective surface at all, yet is
+2950 +- 61 pcm. So either there are two mechanisms, or this one is wrong.

design:
Part of the htgr_sim_v1 execution-architecture epic (bn op-276r). Design
reference: `docs/architecture/htgr-sim-execution.md` §4.2.

The kernel contract (bounded work per invocation) covers **real-time kernels
only**. Two further classes of work are planned and **do not fit it**:

| class | cadence | bounded? | state? | result is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B. Periodic state-carrying** — burnup | every N timesteps | roughly | **yes** — isotopic inventory | updated XS / inventory |
| **C. On-demand calibration** — MC, LIGGGHTS/DEM | user-triggered | **no** — minutes | no | **parameters**, not state |

A criticality calculation or a DEM settling run is unbounded by nature.
**Forcing it into a per-timestep kernel would stall the plant loop; leaving it
undesigned would have it invent its own threading and reintroduce exactly the
problem this epic removes.**

## Requirements

- **Must not block a plant timestep.** Class A's frame budget is the invariant.
  A calibration run that stalls the loop is a defect however good its physics.
- **Cancellable.** A user who triggers a manual calibration and changes their
  mind must not wait minutes; a closed browser tab must not leak a worker.
- **Results arrive as a parameter update** — a *different message class from a
  snapshot*. A snapshot is the whole plant at one instant; a calibration result
  is coefficients valid until superseded. Do not force either into the other's
  shape.
- **Applying a result is explicit and visible.** The plant model changing
  underneath the operator because a background job finished is the same silent
  reinterpretation the multi-thermo epic (#126) forbids elsewhere. Show what was
  applied, when, and from which run.
- **Class B carries state**, so burnup inventory must be **owned explicitly and
  versioned**. A worker holding it implicitly breaks determinism, exactly as the
  worker protocol forbids.
- **Must not starve class A.** In the browser, a long MC run must not consume
  every worker — reserve capacity or use a separate pool.

## Scope of this bead

Design and document the class B/C contract and its integration with the
runtime. **Do not implement the MC or DEM pipelines here** — those are their own
work, and `outram-mc-libs` and `outram-park-fork-liggghts` are separate declared
crates with their own maturity entries.

What this bead owns: the job lifecycle (submit, progress, cancel, complete), the
parameter-update message class, where burnup state lives and how it is versioned,
the scheduling policy that protects the real-time loop, and how a manual
calibration is surfaced to the operator.

## Acceptance

- A long-running job runs to completion **without the plant timestep missing its
  budget**, demonstrated under test.
- The job is cancellable mid-run, and cancellation is observable.
- A parameter update is applied explicitly, with provenance visible in the GUI.
- Burnup state survives a restart and is versioned.

**Depends on:** the worker pool and the protocol — this extends both rather than
duplicating them.

**Branch:** `develop` only. Do not merge or push to `main`.
title: HTGR exec: background job class — periodic burnup and on-demand calibration (MC, DEM)
